settings.enabled_login_help: Show the PoW security challenge inside the Login form.
settings.enabled_signup_help: Show the PoW security challenge inside the Sign Up form.
settings.enabled_forgot_help: Show the PoW security challenge inside the Forgot Password form.
settings.level_help: The work every visitor's browser must do. Times are approximate, measured on a recent PC; phones are 3–6 times slower. With adaptive difficulty enabled, networks that behave suspiciously automatically get up to 8 extra bits (24 bits in total). Every bit doubles the work: levels 4 and 5 are very hard on phones, consider using them only while under attack.
settings.level_2: Level 2 – Balanced (≈ 0.1 s on a PC)
settings.level_3: Level 3 – Strong (≈ 1–3 s on a PC, 5–10 s on a phone, recommended)
settings.level_4: Level 4 – Very strong (≈ 4–12 s on a PC, 20–60 s on a phone)
settings.level_5: Level 5 – Maximum (≈ 15–50 s on a PC, over 1–3 min on a phone: only while under attack)
settings.signup_limit_label: Max registrations per IP every 24 hours
settings.signup_limit_help: Rolling 24-hour limit of accounts that can be created from the same network (IPv6: same /64). 0 = unlimited. Counted only after the account is really created; admin-created accounts are ignored. Only a keyed hash of the network is stored, for 48 hours. Requires correct real-IP detection behind proxies/CDN (see README).
settings.login_limit_label: Max login attempts per IP every 10 minutes
settings.login_limit_help: Beyond this the network is locked out for 15 minutes (also applies to /api/token when protected). 0 = unlimited.
settings.forgot_limit_label: Max password-reset requests per IP every hour
settings.forgot_limit_help: Beyond this the network is locked out for 1 hour. 0 = unlimited.
settings.behavior_checks_help: Rejects or makes harder the requests that look automated: missing/bot User-Agent, missing Accept-Language, cross-site Origin, and a form submitted with no real pointer, keyboard or focus activity. Nothing is stored.
settings.adaptive_help: Automatically raises the difficulty for networks with repeated failed checks or many sign-ups in a few minutes, and for everyone during a site-wide attack. Uses short-lived anonymous counters in the cache; nothing is stored.
settings.protect_token_endpoint_label: Also protect the API login endpoint (/api/token)
settings.protect_token_endpoint_help: Bots can log in by calling /api/token directly, skipping the login form. When enabled, direct calls must carry a CAPTCHA token (GET /api/powcaptcha/challenge?action=token). Turn this off if mobile apps or other integrations log in through the API without a browser.
settings.log_enabled_help: Stores the time, form, outcome and technical reason of recent checks. Only the most recent entries are kept (see the next option for how many).
settings.log_keep_help: How many passed and how many failed checks to keep in the log (so up to twice this number of rows in total). Older entries are deleted automatically, also when you lower this value. Allowed range 10-1000, default 100. Keep it as low as you need: with IP logging enabled, a smaller value means less personal data stored.
settings.log_ip_label: Record and display IP addresses in CAPTCHA logs (warning: GDPR)
settings.log_ip_help: WARNING: an IP address is personal data under the GDPR. By enabling this option you, as data controller, are responsible for having a valid legal basis (e.g. legitimate interest in security), for describing the processing in your privacy policy, for limiting retention and for handling data-subject requests. Non-compliant use may constitute a GDPR violation and lead to penalties. IPs are kept only while the entry is among the most recent events retained (see 'Log entries to keep'), or until the log is cleared. Disabled by default: if you do not need it, leave it off. This is not legal advice; if in doubt, consult a professional.

logs.title: Recent CAPTCHA events
logs.help: The latest {count} successful and {count} failed checks are kept; older entries are deleted automatically. IP addresses are only recorded and displayed if explicitly enabled in the settings.
logs.confirm_clear: Delete all CAPTCHA log entries? This cannot be undone.
logs.ip_banner_enabled: Warning: IP addresses are personal data (GDPR). Make sure you have a legal basis, have disclosed them in your privacy policy and do not keep them longer than necessary. Clear the log when you no longer need it.
logs.ip_banner_disabled: IP addresses are not recorded or displayed (disabled by default for GDPR compliance). To record them, enable the 'Record and display IP addresses in CAPTCHA logs' option in the settings above, after assessing your GDPR obligations.
